clue.text: Mob on boundary with some beer

blocks.note: in cricket, a hit clearing the boundary scores six runs, and the shot is called a six
a mob or crowd is a pack

explanation.surface: A rowdy crowd gathers at the edge of the cricket field with their beer.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'Mob on boundary' puts the mob after the boundary. A six is cricket's biggest scoring hit, over the boundary rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of half a dozen cans sold together, joined by plastic rings, is a standard way to buy beer.

clue.text: List some of the obstacles I met in climbing

indicators.note: only some of the following words' letters are taken, a run hidden inside them
in a down clue, climbing means reading upward, so the run of letters goes backwards

blocks.note: the run spans the end of obstacles, I, met and the start of in

explanation.surface: Someone recounts the hurdles they faced on a mountain ascent.
explanation.definitionFit: To list things is to set them down one by one as separate entries, which is exactly what this verb describes.

clue.text: One objecting to 50% reduction in proper sample

indicators.note: a fifty per cent reduction cuts the word to half its length, keeping its front half

blocks.note: taken as written, then halved
a tester is a small sample, as of perfume in a shop

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the proper sample has been cut in half.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who demonstrates or speaks out against something is voicing an objection, so the noun matches.

clue.text: County clubs replace director — it keeps things tight

indicators.note: replace says one letter takes the place of another within the word

blocks.note: Dorset is a county on England's south coast
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
D is a standard abbreviation for director

explanation.surface: A county's cricket clubs replace their director as a tightening-up measure.
explanation.walkthrough: The C for clubs takes the place of the D for director at the front of Dorset.
explanation.definitionFit: A corset is a close-fitting undergarment that pulls in and shapes the waist, literally holding the body firmly.

clue.text: Investigative assistant takes hour creating current programme

indicators.note: one thing taking another holds it, so a letter is put inside

blocks.note: Dr Watson is Sherlock Holmes's assistant
H is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: A detective's sidekick takes an hour to put together a topical show.
explanation.walkthrough: The H goes in after the first letter of Watson.
explanation.definitionFit: A listings guide of shows and events happening now is the current programme of entertainment.

clue.text: Cooks throw tea into it to make trouble!

indicators.note: to cook something is to tamper with it, as with cooked books, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Kitchen staff fling tea into a pot and cause a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooks' looks like the people in the kitchen, but it is the verb signalling rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in this is an idiom for being in a scrape or facing disapproval and difficulty.

clue.text: Note on wine that's no longer fresh

blocks.note: ti (or te) is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
red is a common shorthand for red wine

explanation.surface: A tasting note on a wine that has gone stale.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'Note on wine' puts the note above the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone worn out and lacking energy is no longer fresh; a stale idea can also be described this way.

clue.text: Heavy individual with sour disposition

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement or placement, so the letters are set out in a new order

blocks.note: a single individual is one
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A weighty person with a grumpy temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposition' reads as temperament, but it signals arranging the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A burdensome duty is described as heavy; both words mean demanding a lot of effort to bear.

clue.text: Spread measures of drink for one who can't hold it?

blocks.note: butter is something spread on bread
a finger is a measure of spirits, the depth of a finger's width in a glass

explanation.surface: Talk of spreads and drinks for someone who can't hold their liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can't hold it' suggests someone who cannot handle drink, but means someone who drops things.
explanation.definitionFit: A clumsy person who keeps dropping things is called this, the question mark marking the playful sense of failing to hold.

clue.text: Go out of your way to be boring about film

indicators.note: being about something means surrounding it, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: dour means gloomy and dull
E.T. is the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: Someone goes to great lengths to be tedious about a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a roundabout route instead of the direct one is literally to go out of your way.

clue.text: Stone's condition, maybe, while search is still ongoing?

definitions.text: Stone's condition, maybe, while search is still ongoing?

blocks.clueFragment: Stone's condition, maybe, while search is still ongoing?
blocks.note: surface reading: the state of a rock, or a person named Stone, during a hunt

blocks.clueFragment: Stone's condition, maybe, while search is still ongoing?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the idiom of a thorough search says no stone is left in this state, so some still are while it goes on

explanation.surface: An update on how a stone is doing while a search continues.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue leans on the idiom 'leave no stone unturned', meaning search everywhere: until the search is over, some stones remain so.
explanation.definitionFit: Not yet flipped over is the state of any stone the searchers have not reached in the proverbial exhaustive hunt.

clue.text: Model order for setter perhaps to settle

blocks.note: first meaning: to pose for an artist
second meaning: a command given to a dog, a setter being a breed of gun dog
third meaning: to come to rest, as a bird on a branch

explanation.walkthrough: The 'setter' looks like the crossword compiler, but here it is the dog, being told what to do.
explanation.definitionFit: The one short verb covers posing for a portrait, the command to a dog, and coming to rest on a perch.

clue.text: Support centre providing source of meat

blocks.note: a rib is a supporting bar, as in a boat's frame
the eye is the centre, as of a storm

explanation.surface: A support centre is where the meat is supplied.
explanation.definitionFit: A steak cut from the rib section of beef is a prized cut, so a supply of meat for the table.

clue.text: Cross section pulled back to reveal hidden entrance

indicators.note: pulling something back draws it the opposite way, so the letters run from right to left

blocks.note: a rood is a crucifix, as on a church's rood screen
a section is a part

explanation.surface: An angry section of a crowd is restrained, uncovering a secret way in.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words together are turned around as one string.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged panel set flush in a floor or ceiling is an opening that can easily go unnoticed.

clue.text: It's the end of a traditional match

definitions.text: It's the end of a traditional match

blocks.clueFragment: It's the end of a traditional match
blocks.note: surface reading: the close of an old-style sporting fixture

blocks.clueFragment: It's the end of a traditional match
blocks.note: setter's reading: a match is a marriage, and traditional vows last until one partner dies

explanation.surface: A commentator marks the finish of an old-fashioned game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' sounds sporting but means a marriage; the traditional vow is 'till death us do part'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the wedding service, the partnership ends only when one spouse dies, so dying ends the union.

clue.text: Idle crowd unlikely to be tolerated in totalitarian states

definitions.text: unlikely to be tolerated in totalitarian states

blocks.note: someone idle is free, with nothing to do
a press is a crowd or throng

explanation.surface: Idle crowds would not be allowed to gather under a dictatorship.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the answer rather than giving a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers able to report without government censorship are something authoritarian regimes typically suppress.

clue.text: Rambling is so grand, but you may need these directions

definitions.note: the answer names signs giving directions

indicators.note: rambling wanders without fixed course, so the letters stray into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Hiking in the countryside is lovely, but you still need guidance on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambling' suggests a country walk, but it signals rearranging the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Boards by the highway pointing to towns and giving distances are how drivers get their route guidance.

clue.text: Tolerance where you are required to follow suit

definitions.text: where you are required to follow suit
definitions.note: a game, described by where its rule applies

blocks.note: first meaning: calm forbearance

blocks.clueFragment: where you are required to follow suit
blocks.note: second meaning: the solo card game, in which cards are built up in order within suits

explanation.walkthrough: 'Follow suit' sounds like copying others, but here it is literal: in the card game, piles must be built by suit. The game is called solitaire in America.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means calm endurance of delay or annoyance, and is also the British name for the one-player card game.

clue.text: Reportedly settled for house name on mad ruin being renovated

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said out loud, so the spoken phrase is heard, not read
something being renovated is being rebuilt, so these letters are reworked into a new order

blocks.note: someone settled has finished wandering, and the phrase said casually drops its final g
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A homeowner restoring a wreck of a cottage picks a name for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Two routes reach the same word: the anagram, and the sound of 'done roamin''. It is a jokey British house name for a retirement bungalow, meaning the owners have finished travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the classic humorous name painted on the gate of a retired couple's home, so it is a house name.

clue.text: Regularly suing peer is not being fair

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; the definition is a participle phrase

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters
a peer is an equal

explanation.surface: Someone keeps taking their colleague to court, which seems unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a lord but means someone of equal standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment that is uneven or unbalanced between parties is unjust, so the adjective matches.

clue.text: Consequence of initiating kettling, as rioters may attack

indicators.note: initiating means starting, so only the opening letter of each word is used

blocks.note: the first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: Police containment tactics provoke a violent backlash from rioters.
explanation.walkthrough: Kettling is a British police tactic of penning protesters into a confined area.
explanation.definitionFit: The idea that actions return to the doer as fate makes this the moral consequence of what one has done.

clue.text: Chopper landing revolutionary in China

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

blocks.note: in cockney rhyming slang, china plate means mate, a friend
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A helicopter carrying a rebel touches down in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopper' and 'landing' paint a helicopter, but the chopper is a blade. 'China' is rhyming slang, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad heavy knife used to hack through vegetation is a tool for chopping, so it is a chopper.

clue.text: Quite right — heart is fluttering

indicators.note: something fluttering moves erratically, so these letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone agrees with feeling as their pulse races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite right' reads as one phrase of agreement; the definition is only the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb meaning fairly or to some degree, it can stand in for quite, as in 'rather good'.

clue.text: No good playing it safe before having a hearty meal

indicators.note: playing with something toys with it, so these letters are moved around

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: Advice that caution is pointless before tucking into a big dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing it safe' is a set phrase, but 'playing' is the signal and 'it safe' the letters. The anagram comes before the two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To dine lavishly on a large spread of food is to eat heartily, so the participles match.

clue.text: Row about large impact noise

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: a spat is a petty quarrel
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: An argument erupts over a large crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' could be a line or a boat trip; here it rhymes with cow and means a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the onomatopoeic word for the wet slapping sound of something hitting a surface.

clue.text: Wine region producing drink in pouch? Au contraire

indicators.note: in puts one thing inside another
French for on the contrary, it flips which piece goes inside which

blocks.note: ale is a drink
a sac is a pouch in an animal or plant

explanation.surface: A wine region turns out drinks served in bags, or the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, the drink goes in the pouch; 'Au contraire' reverses that, so the pouch goes in the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: This north-eastern French province on the Rhine is famous for its white wines, such as Riesling and Gewürztraminer.

clue.text: Take in tenants regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at steady intervals, so every second letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A landlord routinely accepts new lodgers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take in' suggests housing lodgers, but here it means consume.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume food is to take it into the body, so the phrasal verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Name ship after James Joyce?

blocks.note: to dub is to name
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A suggestion to christen a vessel in honour of the Irish novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name ship after' reads as christening a ship, but 'after' places the ship second. Joyce's story collection is titled with the plural form.
explanation.definitionFit: Joyce was born and raised in Ireland's capital, so he is an example of a native of that city.

clue.text: Secret attacker's affectionate partner

blocks.note: first meaning: in the phrase ...-mugger, meaning secret, this word partners mugger, an attacker
second meaning: a partner who embraces a lot

explanation.walkthrough: Hugger-mugger is an old phrase for secrecy or muddle; a mugger is a street attacker, and this word is its partner in the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who embraces others warmly is affectionate, and the word is the first half of the phrase whose second half is a robber.

clue.text: Mess is complete after carnival emptied out

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, so only the outermost letters remain
after places the word before it second in the answer, behind the word that follows

blocks.note: the first and last letters
utter means complete, as in utter nonsense

explanation.surface: After the carnival has cleared, the mess left behind is total.
explanation.definitionFit: An untidy heap of scattered things is a mess; both words describe disorder in a room.

clue.text: Wager outside chance will provide a beefy cut

indicators.note: outside means one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: a wager is a bet
a chance is a risk

explanation.surface: A long-shot bet might win a fine joint of beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside chance' looks like a long shot, but 'outside' is the signal and 'chance' the inner piece.
explanation.definitionFit: This is meat from the breast of a cow, a cut of beef often slow-cooked or braised.
